items.stem: Solve log₂(x + 3) + log₂(x + 6) = 2.
items.markingKey: product law: log₂((x + 3)(x + 6)) = 2 (M1); (x + 3)(x + 6) = 4 (A1); solve the quadratic (M1); reject x = −7 since the logarithms would be undefined (R1); x = −2 (A1).

items.stem: A student claims: "log 8 / log 2 = log 4." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: log 8 / log 2 = log₂ 8 = 3; dividing logs is not the same as the log of a quotient.
items.markingKey: log 8 / log 2 = log₂ 8 = 3; dividing logs is not the same as the log of a quotient. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Solve log₈ x = −1.
Solve 7ˣ = 6^(x + 3), giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
Given that p = log₁₀ x and q = log₁₀ y, express log₁₀(x⁴/∛y²) in terms of p and q.
items.markingKey: quotient law (M1); power law for each term (M1); 4p − 2q/3 (A1 A1).

items.stem:
This question uses the laws of exponents and the definition of a logarithm.
(a) Write 4 as a power of 2.
(b) Hence solve 2^(x + 3) = 4.
(c) Solve 4ˣ = 2^(x + 2).
(d) Find the exact value of log₂ (4 × 2³).
(e) Sketch, on the same axes, y = 2ˣ and y = log₂ x, stating their intercepts and asymptotes.
items.answer: (a) 2² (b) x = −1 (c) x = 2 (d) 5 (e) y = 2ˣ: (0, 1), asymptote y = 0; y = log₂ x: (1, 0), asymptote x = 0
items.markingKey: (a) A1 (b) equate indices (M1) A1 (c) 2^(2x) = 2^(x + 2) (M1); 2x = x + 2 (A1) (d) M1 A1 (e) A1 A1 A1 [Total 10 marks]

items.stem:
The amount A mg of a medicine in a sample is modelled by A = 100e^(−kt), where t is in hours. The half-life is 20.4 hours.
(a) Show that k = ln 2 / 20.4.
(b) Find the amount remaining after 12 hours.
(c) Find the time taken for the amount to fall to 20 mg.
(d) Find the percentage of the substance that remains after each hour.
(e) Explain why the amount never reaches zero according to this model.
items.answer: (a) shown (b) 66.5 mg (c) 47.4 hours (d) 96.7% (e) e^(−kt) > 0 for all t
items.markingKey: (a) ½A₀ = A₀e^(−20.4k) (M1); take ln (A1) AG (b) M1 A1 (c) ln (M1) A1 (d) e^(−k) (M1) A1 (e) R1 [Total 9 marks]

items.stem:
This question investigates products of logarithms.
(a) Prove that logₐb × log_b c = logₐc for positive a, b, c (a, b ≠ 1).
(b) Hence find the exact value of log₂ 5 × log₅ 9 × log₉ 8.
(c) Find the exact value of log₂ 3 × log₃ 4 × log₄ 5 × … × log₆ 7.
(d) Prove that logₐb = 1 / log_b a.
(e) Find the smallest integer n for which log₂ 3 × log₃ 4 × … × logₙ (n + 1) > 10.
items.markingKey: (a) change of base to a common base (M1); cancel (A1) AG (b) chain the result (M1) A1 (c) telescoping product (M1) A1 (d) take c = a (M1) A1 (e) log₂(n + 1) > 10 (M1); n + 1 > 1024 (A1); n = 1024 (A1) [Total 11 marks]

items.stem:
In this question, all answers are exact. Let b = 2.
(a) Write 16 as a power of 2.
(b) Hence solve 2^(x + 3) = 16.
(c) Solve 4ˣ = 2^(x + 4).
(d) Find the exact value of log₂ (16 × 2³).
(e) Sketch, on the same axes, y = 2ˣ and y = log₂ x, stating their intercepts and asymptotes.
items.answer: (a) 2⁴ (b) x = 1 (c) x = 4 (d) 7 (e) y = 2ˣ: (0, 1), asymptote y = 0; y = log₂ x: (1, 0), asymptote x = 0

items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of natural logarithm.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "equation of quadratic type".
items.answer: An equation such as e²ˣ − 5eˣ + 6 = 0 that becomes a quadratic with a substitution such as u = eˣ
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: an equation such as e²ˣ − 5eˣ + 6 = 0 that becomes a quadratic with a substitution such as u = eˣ. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Mohammed writes log₂ 18 / log₂ 2 = log₂ 9. Explain why this is wrong and simplify the quotient correctly.
items.markingKey: A quotient of logarithms is not the logarithm of a quotient (R1); by change of base it equals log₂ 18 (M1 A1).

items.stem: Maya writes (5x⁶)³ = 5x⁹. Explain the errors and simplify correctly.
items.markingKey: The coefficient 5 must also be raised to the power 3 (R1); indices multiply for a power of a power (R1); 125x¹⁸ (A1).

items.stem: Kwame solves e^(2x) − 2eˣ − 24 = 0 and states the solutions x = ln 6 and x = ln(−4). Explain the error and give the correct solution.
items.markingKey: With u = eˣ, u = 6 or u = −4 (M1); eˣ > 0 so eˣ = −4 has no solution and ln of a negative number is undefined (R1); only x = ln 6 (A1).

items.stem: Briefly explain why (−8)^(1/3) is defined but (−8)^(1/2) is not a real number.
items.answer: A cube root of a negative number is real (−2), but no real number squared gives −8.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: A cube root of a negative number is real (−2), but no real number squared gives −8. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Ingrid writes: "(2x)³ = 2x³." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.markingKey: Every factor is cubed: (2x)³ = 8x³. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Freya solves e^(2x) − 5eˣ − 6 = 0 and states the solutions x = ln 6 and x = ln(−1). Explain the error and give the correct solution.
items.markingKey: With u = eˣ, u = 6 or u = −1 (M1); eˣ > 0 so eˣ = −1 has no solution and ln of a negative number is undefined (R1); only x = ln 6 (A1).

items.stem: Without a calculator, find the exact value of (125)^(2/3).
items.markingKey: 3th root of 125 = 5 (M1); raise to the power 2 (M1); 25 (A1).

items.stem: Simplify (5a³b⁻¹)³ ÷ (4a⁻²b⁴), giving your answer with positive indices only.
items.markingKey: Power of a product: each factor raised to the power 3 (M1); subtract indices when dividing (M1); 125a¹¹/(4b⁷) (A1 A1).

items.stem: Solve e^(2x) + 1eˣ − 2 = 0.
items.markingKey: Let u = eˣ: u² + u − 2 = 0 (M1); u = 1 or u = −2 (A1); eˣ = −2 rejected since eˣ > 0 (R1); 0 (A1).

items.stem: Without a calculator, find the exact value of (25)^(1/2).
items.markingKey: 2th root of 25 = 5 (M1); raise to the power 1 (M1); 5 (A1).

items.markingKey: Power of a product: each factor raised to the power 2 (M1); subtract indices when dividing (M1); 9a⁹/b (A1 A1).

items.stem: Solve log₅(x + 4) + log₅(x + 24) = 3.
items.markingKey: product law: log₅((x + 4)(x + 24)) = 3 (M1); (x + 4)(x + 24) = 125 (A1); solve the quadratic (M1); reject x = −29 since the logarithms would be undefined (R1); x = 1 (A1).
